sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'zookeeper' AND ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AND ts < '2015-08-26 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'zookeeper' AND ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AND ts < '2015-08-26 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'zookeeper' AND start_ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2015-08-26 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'zookeeper' AND start_ts >= '2015-07-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2015-07-29 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'zookeeper' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'zookeeper' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'zookeeper' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ) SELECT *, count(*) OVER () AS candidates FROM base ORDER BY bursts DESC, nodes DESC, pattern_id LIMIT 15

Block `blk_-1608999687919862906` was written, copied to 10 datanodes, read many times, and then deleted. It has no errors: all 269 lines are INFO, and there are no WARN or ERROR lines. The lines fall into two sessions, split by a gap of about an hour.

**Session 1: write, replication and reads (2008-11-09 20:35:18 to 20:36:26, 249 lines)**
1. **20:35:18, allocation.** The NameNode (`dfs.FSNamesystem`) allocated the block for `/mnt/hadoop/mapred/system/job_200811092030_0001/job.jar`. This is a MapReduce job jar. The DataNodes began "Receiving block" at the same moment, starting with 10.250.19.102.
2. **20:35:19, initial pipeline.** Three datanodes (10.250.19.102, 10.250.10.6 and 10.250.14.224) received the block, 91,178 bytes. Their PacketResponders terminated, and the NameNode recorded the first replicas in its block map (`addStoredBlock`).
3. **20:35:21 to 20:35:28, replication chain.** The NameNode asked replica holders to copy the block onward. Each copy was followed by a "Starting thread to transfer", a "Transmitted block" and a new `addStoredBlock` line:
   - 10.250.14.224 copied to 10.251.215.16 and 10.251.71.193.
   - 10.251.215.16 copied to 10.251.74.79 and 10.251.107.19.
   - 10.251.107.19 copied to 10.251.31.5 and 10.251.71.240.
   
   The NameNode logged 10 `addStoredBlock` lines in total. I did not read the last one or two individually.
4. **From 20:35:23 to 20:36:26, reads.** The block was read heavily. There are 203 "Served block … to /client" lines in all, which is 75% of the block's lines. They start at 20:35:23, are densest around 20:35:27, and continue until 20:36:26. This fits a job jar being fetched by many task nodes.

**Session 2: deletion (2008-11-09 21:38:09 to 21:38:40, 20 lines)**
5. **21:38:09, invalidation.** The NameNode logged `NameSystem.delete` and added the block to the `invalidSet` of 10 datanodes: 10.250.10.6, 10.250.14.224, 10.251.107.19, 10.251.111.209, 10.251.215.16, 10.251.31.5, 10.251.71.193, 10.251.71.240, 10.251.74.79 and 10.251.90.64. That matches the 10 replicas created earlier.
6. **21:38:10 to 21:38:40, file removal.** Each datanode logged `dfs.FSDataset: Deleting block … file /mnt/hadoop/dfs/data/current/blk_-1608999687919862906`. That is 10 deletions, about 30 seconds after the invalidation.

This is a normal block lifecycle, probably a job jar that was cleaned up when its job finished (my inference, not stated in the logs). The replication factor looks much higher than the HDFS default of 3, which is common for job jars.

The ordering above comes from timestamps. Several events share the same second.

**Zookeeper problems that recurred most, 2015-07-29 to 2015-08-26**

Two teams own all 11 problem patterns in the window: coordination-platform and client-connectivity. A "burst" below means a pattern that reappears after more than 30 quiet minutes. These are recurrences of log patterns, not confirmed incidents.

| Rank | Pattern | Component | Owner | Bursts | Lines |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "caught end of stream exception" (WARN) | NIOServerCnxn | client-connectivity | 18 | 1,670 |
| 2 | "Cannot open channel to N at election address" (WARN) | QuorumCnxManager | coordination-platform | 8 | 2,584 |
| 3 | "Unexpected Exception:" (ERROR) | NIOServerCnxn | client-connectivity | 9 | 27 |
| 4 | "Unexpected exception causing shutdown while sock still open" (ERROR) | LearnerHandler | coordination-platform | 7 | 590 |
| 5 | "Exception when following the leader" (WARN) | Follower | coordination-platform | 6 | 11 |
| 6 | "Connection broken for id N, my id = N" (WARN) | RecvWorker | coordination-platform | 6 | 32 |
| 7 | "Unexpected exception, tries=N, connecting to /IP" (WARN) | Learner | coordination-platform | 5 | 8 |

The ranking is the priority score, which weighs bursts, trend, spread, persistence and severity.

Smaller patterns sit below these. One is "ZooKeeperServer not running" session closes (159 lines, 2 bursts). Another is a single burst of 10,356 "Connection broken for id…" lines.

**By team**
- **coordination-platform** has 7 problem patterns, 35 bursts and about 13.6k lines. It owns the quorum and election layer.
- **client-connectivity** has 4 problem patterns, 30 bursts and about 1.9k lines. It owns the client-session layer.

**Caveats**
- Every pattern shows 0 bursts in the previous period and is flagged "new". This is probably because the corpus begins on 2015-07-29, not because they are truly new.
- Zookeeper logs carry no host, so I can't say which ensemble member is affected.
- Cost, downtime and root cause are not in these logs.

**What to investigate first**
1. **The 2015-07-29 event, owned by coordination-platform.**
   - It is the biggest event in the window. Of 48.5k WARN lines in the window, 42.7k fall on 07-29 alone.
   - The first problem line is "Unexpected exception causing shutdown while sock still open" at 19:03:35 (LearnerHandler, ERROR), followed by 580 "GOODBYE" lines.
   - At 19:04:02 a storm of about 10,358 "Received connection request / Connection broken / Interrupting SendWorker / Send worker leaving thread" lines runs until 19:37.
   - Client-side "Connection reset by peer" and "ZooKeeperServer not running" session closes appear around 19:53.
   - This looks like a leader or learner connection failure followed by quorum reconnect churn. That is a hypothesis, since earlier in time does not prove cause.
   - Check what happened to the leader or network around 19:03, and why peers kept reconnecting for 30 minutes.
2. **"Cannot open channel to N at election address".** It is the most persistent pattern, active in all 5 weeks, and it points to a peer that is unreachable or down during election. Check network, DNS and firewall between members, and whether a member is repeatedly restarting.
3. **Later, smaller flare-ups.** WARN volume returned on 08-10, 08-20 and especially 08-24 and 08-25 (1,039 and 1,404 lines). Check whether these are the same quorum-connection pattern, and how they relate to the 07-29 event.
4. **client-connectivity, second.** "caught end of stream exception" has the most bursts (18). The client-side session closes at 19:53 on 07-29 look like fallout from the quorum event. Check whether the later bursts are also tied to the quorum problems or are independent, for example client timeouts or load balancers. Also look at the 27 "Unexpected Exception" ERROR lines, which have the highest severity.

**Priority for the next period: the "script not found or unable to stat" errors, then the mod_jk / jk2 worker errors.** Both groups were worse or still active in 2005-12-01 → 2006-03-01. The log ends on 2006-02-28, so the window is effectively 13 weeks. Logs don't give cost, downtime, customer impact or root cause, so this is a ranking by what the logs measure.

**1. "script not found or unable to stat" (web-platform, httpd). Highest priority.**
- It appears as two patterns, 300042 and 300033, which score 89.5 and 84.2 in the priority ranking.
- Pattern 300042 has 3,339 lines in 127 bursts, up from 29 bursts in the previous quarter (+98).
- Pattern 300033 has 2,207 lines in 77 bursts, up from 32 (+45). It names the client IP and the path, so it can be traced.
- The stored judgment calls both "job or application failure".
- Hypothesis, not confirmed: a missing or misconfigured CGI script, or a probe for scripts that don't exist. Checking the paths and client IPs with `top_entities` would tell these apart.
- The same message from mod_jk (pattern 300046) is smaller, at 263 lines and 24 bursts, but also rising (+7).

**2. mod_jk / jk2 worker errors (app-integration). Second priority.**
- "jk2_init() Can't find child N in scoreboard" (pattern 300022) ranks #2 (score 87.5). It is the most persistent problem, active in 13 of 14 weeks, with 415 lines in 69 bursts (+15).
- "mod_jk child workerEnv in error state" (pattern 300040) has 1,623 lines in 71 bursts. That is down from 160 bursts, so it is improving but still frequent.
- This looks like the Apache–Tomcat connector being unhealthy. It is my reading of the pattern names, not something the logs confirm.

**3. Worker.jni / channel.jni startup failures (web-platform). Lower priority, but check.**
- About ten patterns, such as "config.update(): Can't create worker.jni:onStartup" and "env.createBean2(): Factory error…", each have 11 lines and 11 bursts.
- They are falling (16 bursts in the previous period, 11 now) and rank #4–#10 only because they appear every week they are active.
- The identical counts suggest one repeated event, probably a restart or reconfiguration with a broken JNI worker config. That is a hypothesis. One configuration fix would likely clear all of them.

**Lower priority or noise**
- "Directory index forbidden by rule" is the busiest pattern, with 1,650 lines in 853 bursts, but it is falling (−192). The stored judgment labels it "not a problem" (fault probability 0.12), although its threat score is 0.66. It looks like scanning or probing that the server is correctly refusing. I'd route it to security review rather than treat it as an outage.
- "File does not exist … %…c.." (pattern 300028) is small, at 22 lines, and looks like probing.

**Context**
- Volume is uneven. Weeks of 2005-12-12, 12-19 and 12-26 had only 48 lines each, which looks like a quiet or logging gap. Roughly 3,000–3,800 lines a week resumed from mid-January, so the late-period error rates are the relevant ones.
- Apache logs have no host field, so I can't say whether the problems are on one server or several.
- By team, web-platform has 17 problem patterns and app-integration has 3. Total bursts fell for both: web-platform 1,331 → 1,205 and app-integration 231 → 164. The rise is concentrated in the script-not-found patterns.

**Suggested next steps**
1. List the top paths and client IPs for the script-not-found errors.
2. Check the mod_jk worker and scoreboard configuration and the Tomcat connection.
3. Fix the JNI worker config.
4. Pass the directory-index and File-does-not-exist probing to security-ops.

From 2018-01-01 to 2018-01-08, the SSH server (LabSZ) logged **102,039 failed-password lines for root**. They came from **214 distinct IP addresses**, and eight of those addresses account for most of them.

**Top sources (log lines per IP):**

| IP | Lines | Active window |
|---|---|---|
| 59.63.188.30 | 28,766 | Jan 3 – Jan 5 |
| 183.63.110.206 | 17,340 | Jan 2 – Jan 3 |
| 58.242.83.25 | 14,383 | Jan 1 – Jan 2 |
| 183.192.189.131 | 8,670 | Jan 3 |
| 218.65.30.30 | 8,374 | Jan 1 – Jan 2 |
| 218.87.109.156 | 7,135 | Jan 3 – Jan 4 |
| 182.100.67.120 | 6,179 | Jan 1 – Jan 2 |
| 182.100.67.52 | 3,389 | Jan 4 – Jan 5 |

Those eight sum to about 94,200 lines, roughly 92% of the total.

**Smaller sources:**
- Ten addresses had roughly 250–620 lines each: 183.192.189.133, 139.219.239.13, 123.235.32.19, 119.7.221.129, 60.2.12.12, 115.238.230.180, 114.112.48.155, 119.1.109.20, 218.65.30.123 and 218.65.30.43.
- The rest of the 214 addresses each had fewer lines.
- Several come from the same ranges as the big ones: 218.65.30.x, 182.100.67.x and 183.192.189.x. That suggests the same operators rotating addresses.

**Reading the counts:**
- The counts are log lines, not exact login attempts. About 35% of the lines (35,393) are "message repeated N times: [Failed password for root …]" summaries. Each of those stands for several attempts but counts as one line.
- Only 66,646 lines are individual failed-password events. The true number of attempts is therefore higher than 102,039.
- I did not expand the repeat counts, so I can't give an exact attempt total.
- I matched the text "Failed password root", so invalid-user or other failure types are not included.
- The per-IP counts come from the top-30 listing. The other 184 addresses are not itemised.

The pattern looks like brute-force or credential-stuffing bursts. Each address was active for hours to about two days, then stopped, and a new one took over.
